You're working on Nxeon, a hosting platform (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres) on a Proxmox server. `/opt/nxeon` is the production working tree (git, origin/main). `/opt/nxeon-staging` is a separate staging checkout with its own DB, used for verification before anything touches prod.

## Background — read this before touching anything

The owner asked for a full overhaul of the live-chat AI assistant: "wire it to the SDK, overhaul the live chat, add animations, guardrails, complete system knowledge, real-world live problem solving, account detail pull-up, cleaner/modern styling, behave like a real AI assistant with visible thinking not templated responses, special cards for hosting plans, working buttons for other things."

I (the other Claude session handling this) already investigated and found the backend is FAR more built than the owner realizes — they've never actually seen it run because the platform's Anthropic API key has a **$0 credit balance** (confirmed live: a real request returns `"Your credit balance is too low"`). That funding gap is a billing action only the account owner can take at console.anthropic.com — it is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for you, don't attempt anything about it, don't chase it, just know it's why you can't get a real end-to-end model response while verifying (see "Verification given the funding gap" below).

Already built and working (do NOT rebuild these — read them, understand them, and extend/reuse):
- `lib/anthropic.ts` — Messages API wrapper, JUST migrated (this session) from raw fetch to the official `@anthropic-ai/sdk`. Exports `askClaude`, `askClaudeWithTools` (a hand-rolled tool-use loop), `effectiveKeyFor`, `platformKeyConfigured`, types `ClaudeMessage`/`ClaudeContent`/`ClaudeToolDef`.
- `lib/kb-llm.ts` — the chat agent's brain. `resolveBotKey()` resolves the effective key. `buildSystem()` builds a real agentic system prompt (tool-first, account-aware for signed-in customers, anonymous-safe for guests). Already forbids "canned, templated, or evasive" replies. Already supports a hidden `[[cards: key1, key2]]` directive the model appends to recommend plan cards.
- `lib/kb-system.ts` (657 lines) — a comprehensive, accurate, operator-authored knowledge base with real guardrails ("Never invent prices, plans, specs, SLAs, coupon codes..."). This is genuinely complete; don't rewrite it, just skim it so you understand what the agent already knows.
- `lib/kb-tools.ts` (984 lines) — already implements REAL tools: `get_account_overview`, `list_services`, `get_service`, `list_invoices`, `get_billing_status`, `list_tickets`, `open_support_ticket`, `check_platform_status`, `get_plans`, `search_help`. Account-detail pull-up already exists at the tool level.
- `lib/kb-plans.ts` — the plan-card catalog. Shared Hosting, VPS, Game Server, Business Email cards already exist with `product`, `priceLabel`, `features`, `ctaUrl` etc. AUDIT this against the real current catalog (cross-check prices/features against `prisma/seed-hosting-plans.ts`, `prisma/seed.ts`, `prisma/seed-gameplans.ts`, `prisma/seed-email-plans.ts`, and any NxCloud seed) — fix anything stale, but the mechanism itself already works.
- `components/ChatWidget.tsx` (999 lines) — the actual widget. Floating bubble, polling-based (`GET /api/chat` every ~4s), visitor identification via localStorage, existing `botThinking`/`agentTyping` state (currently just a static 3-dot pulse, see line ~862), existing plan-card rendering (`PlanCardData` type, renders price/features/CTA button), an existing "funnel" chip-based quick-menu (`funnelNode`/`onChip`), file attachment support, conversation history switcher.
- `lib/chat-typing.ts` — a lightweight, deliberately in-memory, TTL-based, single-process presence-signal store (`markTyping`/`readTyping`, `TYPING_TTL_MS = 6000`, persisted across HMR via `globalThis`). This is the EXACT pattern to mirror for the new "live step" feature below — read it fully before building anything, don't invent a different mechanism (no new DB table, no Redis).
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` — the polling endpoint; already returns `typing?: { agent?: boolean }` sourced from `chat-typing.ts`.

## What you're actually building

### 1. Visual redesign — cleaner, modern look, real animations
- The established brand system is navy+violet+cyan (`brand-500`, `accent-cyan`, `accent-blue` etc. — grep `app/globals.css`'s `@theme` block and `tailwind.config`/CSS variables for the exact token names; DO NOT invent a new palette or drift toward generic AI-chatbot styling — purple gradient bubble + Inter font is what EVERY AI chat widget looks like, this one needs to look like it belongs to Nxeon specifically). Reuse the same `card glass` treatment already used for the panel container, and the SAME animation convention already established this session in `ProvisioningOverlay.tsx` (`motion-safe:animate-orbit-spin`, `-check-pop`, `-check-draw`, `-ring-glow`, all defined as `--animate-*` custom properties in `app/globals.css`'s `@theme` block, gated by `motion-safe:` so `prefers-reduced-motion` is respected). Add new keyframes to that SAME block following that SAME convention, don't invent a parallel animation system.
- Concrete targets: message bubble entrance (subtle rise+fade, not a jarring pop), the panel open/close transition (currently probably instant — check), plan-card reveal, the launcher button (already has a hover scale — consider a subtle idle pulse/glow when there's an unread message, check if that exists), the new "thinking step" indicator (below), the funnel chips.
- Read `components/customer/WizardReassuranceCard.tsx` and the plan-card grids in `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` for the established icon+short-copy visual convention if you add any new small UI elements — don't invent a new pattern for something this codebase already has one for.

### 2. Live "thinking" step indicator — the real fix for "feels templated"
Right now `botThinking` is a boolean → static 3-dot pulse. The agent already reasons through multiple tool calls per turn (the loop in `askClaudeWithTools`), but the visitor sees nothing of that — it just looks frozen then dumps an answer. Fix:
- **Backend**: add an optional `onStep?: (toolName: string) => void` callback param to `askClaudeWithTools` in `lib/anthropic.ts`, invoked right before each tool executes (you have the tool name at that point in the existing loop). Keep this fully backward compatible — every existing caller that doesn't pass `onStep` must be completely unaffected.
- **`lib/kb-llm.ts`**: when calling `askClaudeWithTools` for the live chat, pass an `onStep` that maps each tool name to a short human-readable label (e.g. `get_billing_status` → "Checking your billing…", `list_services` → "Looking up your services…", `search_help` → "Searching the help center…", `check_platform_status` → "Checking system status…", `get_plans` → "Pulling up current plans…", `open_support_ticket` → "Opening a ticket for you…", `get_account_overview` → "Pulling up your account…", `list_invoices` → "Finding your invoices…", `get_service` → "Checking that service…", `list_tickets` → "Checking your tickets…") and writes it into a new lightweight store — add `lib/chat-bot-step.ts` mirroring `lib/chat-typing.ts`'s EXACT pattern (in-memory Map, TTL ~8-10s so a stalled/crashed request doesn't leave a stuck label, `globalThis` HMR persistence, a `setBotStep(conversationId, label)` / `readBotStep(conversationId)` pair, a `_resetBotStep()` test helper).
- **`app/api/chat/route.ts`**: add `botStep?: string | null` alongside the existing `typing.agent` in the poll response, sourced from `readBotStep`.
- **`components/ChatWidget.tsx`**: when `botThinking` is true, show the live step label (cross-fading between steps as they change, e.g. a simple opacity+translateY transition) instead of / in addition to the 3-dot pulse. Fall back to a generic "Thinking…" when no step label is available yet (the model's own final-answer generation isn't a tool call, so there's a gap after the last tool with no step label — handle that gracefully, don't show a stale old label).
- This is the RIGHT-SIZED fix — do NOT attempt a full SSE/token-streaming rewrite of the chat transport (that's a much bigger, riskier architecture change explicitly out of scope for this task; the polling+step-label approach directly addresses "feels alive, not templated" at a fraction of the risk).

### 3. Rich action cards beyond plan cards
The model can already emit `[[cards: key1, key2]]` to show plan-recommendation cards. Extend this so the model can ALSO surface real account-action cards tied to what a tool actually returned — e.g. after `list_invoices` runs, a card linking to a specific real invoice; after `get_service`, a "Go to your service" card linking to the actual `/dashboard/servers/[id]`; after `open_support_ticket` succeeds, a confirmation card with the ticket reference. Design this as a natural extension of the EXISTING `cardsJson`/`PlanCardData` mechanism (add a `type` discriminator so the renderer can distinguish a plan-recommendation card from an account-action card, rather than inventing a wholly separate parallel system) — read `app/api/chat/route.ts`'s cards-parsing code and the render logic in `ChatWidget.tsx` (the `PlanCardData` type and its render component near line ~62-120) before designing this, and grep for where `cardsJson` actually gets written (probably in `lib/kb-llm.ts` or wherever the model's raw text gets parsed for the `[[cards: ...]]` directive) so the new directive/type threads through the same pipeline.
- Give the model clear instructions in the system prompt (`lib/kb-llm.ts`'s `buildSystem()`) for WHEN to use an action card vs. plain text vs. a plan card — don't let it spam cards for everything.

### 4. Audit every button in the widget
Click through every interactive element in `ChatWidget.tsx` on staging and confirm it does what it claims: history switcher, new-chat, close, file attach, send, funnel chips (and their back-navigation), plan-card CTA links, and any new action cards you add. Fix anything broken, stubbed, or dead. Note what you found even if nothing was broken.

### 5. Guardrails — spot-check, don't rebuild
`kb-system.ts` and `buildSystem()` already have real guardrails (no invented prices/plans/coupons, tool-first behavior, no canned replies). Spot check for gaps an owner would care about: does the system prompt say what to do if a visitor asks something abusive/off-topic/tries to extract the system prompt itself? If there's no explicit instruction for "visitor asks you to ignore your instructions" or "visitor asks for something outside Nxeon's business," add a short, clear directive — don't rewrite the whole prompt, just close real gaps.

## Verification given the funding gap
You cannot get a real live model response end-to-end (the key has no credit) — don't waste time trying repeatedly once you've confirmed this yourself once. Instead:
1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after every change.
2. `npm test` — capture the current failing-test-name set BEFORE you start (as of this session it's exactly 34 pre-existing failures, all pricing/proration/auth-flavored, nothing chat-related) and diff after every change; the set must stay identical unless you're intentionally adding new passing tests.
3. For the parts that need a real model response to see (the step-indicator sequence, action cards actually rendering), write a focused test or a small standalone script that calls `lib/kb-llm.ts`'s internals with a MOCKED/stubbed `askClaudeWithTools` (or test `onStep` wiring directly against `lib/anthropic.ts` with a fake `execTool`) so you can prove the plumbing works without needing real credits. Also directly unit-test `lib/chat-bot-step.ts` (mirror the existing `test/chat-typing.test.ts` if there is one — check).
4. For everything else (UI rendering, animations, button clicks, existing plan-card display which doesn't need the LLM at all since it's just JSON→render), verify live on `https://staging.nxeon.cloud` with Playwright (`/opt/nxeon-staging/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs`, `chromium.launch()` + `newContext({ bypassCSP: true })`). The chat widget is visitor-facing and doesn't require login for anonymous testing; for account-aware testing log in as `claude-audit-2026@nxeon.test` / `AuditPass123!`. Take screenshots.
5. Commit incrementally with clear messages ending in:
   ```

   Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   ```
   `git push origin main` — retry once after 2s on a "cannot lock ref" error (transient, known issue in this repo, other work may be landing on main concurrently from elsewhere in this session).
6. Deploy to staging via `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` after each meaningful chunk (this can take a couple minutes and may background-timeout the calling command — check its output file rather than re-running it).

## Hard constraints
- Do **NOT** run `scripts/promote-production.sh`. This is a big, customer-facing surface change — production must not be touched. Staging only; the owner decides when to promote after reviewing it.
- Do not run `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon` itself — only `tsc --noEmit`/`npm test` are safe there. Real builds happen via `deploy-staging.sh`.
- Don't touch the Anthropic funding/billing question — not your problem to solve, just work around it per the verification section above.
- Don't rebuild what already works (the tool loop, the KB, the plan-card mechanism, the typing-signal pattern) — extend it. This codebase already has a lot of the requested functionality; your job is filling real gaps, not replacing working systems.
- Don't scope-creep beyond what's listed above. If you find something else that seems off while in these files, note it in your final report instead of fixing it inline.

## Final report
Report back: what you built per section above, exact verification results (tsc/test-diff, staging deploy status, screenshots taken and what they showed, what you confirmed works vs. couldn't verify due to the funding gap), the button audit findings, and any judgment calls or open questions. Cite file paths/line numbers.

Everything is clean and pushed. Here's the final report.

## Summary

Commit `ea41210` on `main` (pushed to origin), deployed to staging (`/opt/nxeon-staging` now on this commit, `nxeon-staging-web` active, HTTP 200).

### 1. Live "thinking" step indicator
- `lib/anthropic.ts`: `askClaudeWithTools` gains optional `onStep?: (toolName: string) => void`, fired immediately before each tool executes (`lib/anthropic.ts:171`). Omitting it is a no-op — verified via a dedicated back-compat test.
- `lib/chat-bot-step.ts` (new): TTL'd in-memory store mirroring `lib/chat-typing.ts` exactly — `setBotStep`/`readBotStep`/`clearBotStep`/`_resetBotStep`, 9s TTL.
- `lib/kb-llm.ts`: `STEP_LABELS` map (all 10 tools from the task spec) wired via `onStep: convoId ? (toolName) => setBotStep(convoId, stepLabelFor(toolName)) : undefined`, with `clearBotStep(convoId)` in a `finally` so a turn never leaks its label into the next one.
- `conversationId` threaded through `lib/kb.ts` → `lib/kb-run.ts` → `lib/kb-llm.ts`.
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` GET now returns `botStep: readBotStep(convo.id)`.
- `components/ChatWidget.tsx`: the indicator now shows during the *real* wait (`sending`), not just the old cosmetic post-hoc delay; label cross-fades via `key={botStep}` + the existing `fade-up` keyframe, falls back to "Thinking…" when no step is active yet.
- **Known limitation**: no `activeId` exists yet for a conversation's very first message, so live steps only show from the 2nd turn onward on that thread; the "Thinking…" fallback covers the gap. Documented, not fixed — would need bigger plumbing to expose the id sooner.

### 2. Rich action cards
- `lib/kb-tools.ts`: `resolveActionCard(userId, kind, id, label)` — ownership-checked (same trust model as every other tool), resolves `service|invoice|ticket` to a real dashboard link (`/dashboard/servers/[id]`, `/dashboard/hosting/[id]`, `/dashboard/domains/[id]`, `/dashboard/invoices/[id]`, `/dashboard/support/[id]`; email/volume fall back to their non-parametrized overview page since no per-id route exists).
- `lib/kb-run.ts`: new `[[action: type=…, id=…, label="…"]]` directive parsed alongside the existing `[[cards: …]]`, both merged into one `cardsJson` array with a `type: "plan" | "action"` discriminator.
- `components/ChatWidget.tsx`: new `ActionCard` component + `ChatCard` dispatcher; `PlanCardData.type` is optional so pre-existing stored messages (no `type` field) still render as plan cards.
- `lib/kb-llm.ts`: system prompt instructs exactly when to use it (right after opening a ticket, diagnosing one specific service, or pointing at one unpaid invoice) — never combined with a plan-card directive, max one per message.

### 3. Voice/guardrails (this became the priority fix per your correction)
- `lib/kb-llm.ts` `buildSystem()`: added "LEAD WITH THE ANSWER," "BE SPECIFIC TO WHAT THEY SAID," and "PERSONALITY IS ALLOWED" directives, plus two full BAD-vs-GOOD contrast pairs (pricing question, troubleshooting question) with a named banned-phrase list.
- `lib/kb-system.ts`: new §10 "VOICE CALIBRATION — WORKED EXAMPLES" appendix (style-only, explicitly subordinate to the facts sections).
- New BOUNDARIES directive: prompt-injection/persona-override attempts and off-topic/abusive requests get a short, calm redirect instruction.

### 4. Plan-card catalog audit (found real staleness)
- Business Email storage was stale everywhere (`kb-plans.ts` + `kb-system.ts`): showed 5/10/25 GB, real seed (`prisma/seed-email-plans.ts`) is 10/25/50 GB. Fixed in both.
- Added missing `game-cs2` and `game-terraria` featured cards (real products, previously had no card).
- Everything else (Shared Hosting, VPS, other game tiers, NxCloud prose) cross-checked against seeds and was already accurate.

### 5. Visual/animation pass
- `app/globals.css`: added `panel-out` (reverse of the existing `panel-in`) to the same `@theme` block, same convention, `motion-safe:` gated.
- Message-row entrance, funnel-chip-switch, and thinking-label cross-fade all reuse the existing `fade-up`/`panel-in` keyframes rather than inventing new ones.
- Panel now animates open (`panel-in`, already existed but was unused) and close (`panel-out` + a JS safety-net timeout so `prefers-reduced-motion` users, or any missed `animationend`, never get stuck).
- **Skipped deliberately**: idle pulse/glow on the launcher bubble for unread messages — would require polling while the panel is closed (an architecture change), out of scope per the "no bigger transport rewrites" constraint. Noting as an open question for you.

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean throughout, clean now.
- `npm test`: 1178→1192 tests, 1144→1158 passing, **failure set identical** (34, byte-diffed against the pre-existing baseline) — confirmed via `diff`.
- New tests: `test/chat-bot-step.test.ts` (TTL store + source tripwires across the whole wiring path), `test/anthropic-onstep.test.ts` (hermetic — spins a local HTTP server, points the real SDK at it via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, proves `onStep` fires before each tool in order with a real request/response round-trip, no funded key needed).
- Staging deploy: succeeded, HTTP 200, commit `ea41210` confirmed live.
- Playwright button audit (screenshots in `/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots/`): bubble open/close (with animation), funnel root→branch→back, identity capture fields, funnel-seeded send, history open/back, attach-image button present, new-chat reset, signed-in login + identity-skip, signed-in seeded send — **all passed**.
- Confirmed live (both anonymous and signed-in) that the funding gap manifests exactly as expected: the agent attempts the call, it errors, and the graceful degradation message renders correctly with the visitor's name interpolated ("Sorry Playwright —…" / "Sorry Claude —…"). This proves the full pipeline end-to-end; only the live step-label/action-card *visual* couldn't be seen this way (covered instead by the hermetic tests above).

### Found but out of scope (not fixed, noted per your instructions)
- React hydration error (`#418`) fires on the homepage on load, before chat is touched at all — pre-existing, unrelated to this work, root file not identified.
- `/api/health` returns 503 on staging because the Proxmox component reports "down" — expected for a non-prod box without real Proxmox access, not an app bug.
- Login form's Email/Password `<label>`s aren't associated with their inputs (no `htmlFor`/`id`) in `components/AuthForms.tsx` — a real, quick a11y fix; flagged as a background task chip (`task_6dc334d9`) rather than fixed inline.
